steps.tx: **Protein-energy wasting**, abbreviated as **PEW**, in chronic kidney disease is characterized by simultaneous loss of systemic somatic **muscle mass** and **visceral protein** reserves, driven by chronic uremic anorexia, persistent low-grade **inflammation**, and metabolic acidosis. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: The **KDOQI 2020** guidelines recommend dietary protein restriction of **0.55** to **0.60** g/kg/day, or very-low-protein diets of **0.28** to **0.43** g/kg/day supplemented with **ketoacid analogues**, in stable non-diabetic **CKD stages 3 to 5** to retard progression. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: In contrast to pre-dialysis restriction, patients undergoing maintenance **hemodialysis** and **peritoneal dialysis** require increased **dietary protein** of **1.0** to **1.2** g/kg/day to compensate for substantial dialytic amino acid and protein losses. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
steps.say: In contrast to pre-dialysis restriction, patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis require increased dietary protein of 1 point 0 to 1 point 2 g/kg/day to compensate for substantial dialytic amino acid and protein losses. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Pre-Dialysis CKD (Stages 3-5)
points: Protein target: Restricted to 0.55 to 0.60 g/kg/day
Pathophysiologic goal: Lower uremic toxins and hyperfiltration

right.title: Maintenance Dialysis (HD / PD)
points: Protein target: Elevated to 1.0 to 1.2 g/kg/day
Pathophysiologic goal: Compensate for dialytic protein losses
Peritoneal loss: Up to 5 to 15 g protein lost daily in effluent
Clinical outcome: Higher protein intake reduces mortality

steps.tx: **Comprehensive conservative kidney management**, designated as **CCKM**, provides planned, holistic, patient-centered care for advanced kidney disease without dialysis, prioritizing **symptom control**, psychological support, and advanced care planning. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.

steps.tx: Comparative studies in **frail elderly** patients aged over **75** to **80** years with a **Charlson Comorbidity Index** of at least **8** show that **CCKM** achieves equivalent survival compared to dialysis, with fewer hospitalizations and superior home time. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Uremic pruritus** affects **40%** to **50%** of patients with advanced CKD. It is effectively relieved by **difelikefalin**, a selective peripheral **kappa-opioid** receptor agonist, or centrally acting **gabapentin** and pregabalin. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Nutritional screening relies on validated clinical scoring instruments. The **Subjective Global Assessment**, or **SGA**, and the **Malnutrition-Inflammation Score**, or **MIS**, are recommended for regular periodic screening of nutritional status and PEW. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Subjective Global Assessment (SGA)
points: Components: Dietary history, weight changes, gastrointestinal symptoms
Physical exam: Subcutaneous fat and muscle wasting

right.title: Malnutrition-Inflammation Score (MIS)
points: Components: 10 quantitative components combining SGA and laboratory
Biomarkers: Serum albumin and total iron-binding capacity
Utility: Strongest independent predictor of dialysis mortality

steps.tx: **Restless legs syndrome**, or **RLS**, in uremic patients exhibits nocturnal exacerbation and correlates with iron deficiency. First-line pharmacotherapy utilizes low-dose **gabapentin**, pregabalin, or intravenous **iron replacement**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.
